changes.evidence: Wrong order. Daredevil S3 tells Dex's past: after Eileen Mercer's death he joined the U.S. Army, left it, worked at the suicide hotline, then joined the FBI (episodes 5-6; his Army service also comes up in therapy and in Fisk's talk with him). In episode 6 the FBI makes him step down and hand over his badge, and that same night Fisk recruits him (episodes 6-8). Turns on Fisk in episode 13. As filed, the stages read as if he left Fisk's Empire for the FBI and then the FBI for the Army. The Army is a past group and goes first; FBI next; Fisk's Empire after. Same groups, reordered.

Daredevil S1: Vanessa is an art dealer at Scene Contempo Gallery. She sells Fisk 'Rabbit in a Snowstorm' there in episode 3, he comes back to ask her out in episode 4, and Matt visits her there in episode 9. The name is said on screen in episode 9 (Karen: 'It says she works at Scene Contempo Gallery'). Daredevil: Born Again S2 episode 5 flashbacks show the same job. A real workplace counts as a group. A verifier already confirmed this in an earlier pass (svout_2), but it has not been applied.

In Daredevil S1 Nobu sits at Fisk's table as the representative of 'those I speak for' (episode 1 onward; 'Remember your promise to me and those I speak for', episode 5). In episode 9 he fights Matt in the Hand's uniform. Daredevil S2 then shows and tells that he was the Hand's man all along and that the Yakuza was a front. Settled rule: a past group the screen tells counts, keyed to the first title, so the Hand belongs in S1, ahead of his seat in Fisk's alliance. The S2 stage stays: Fisk's empire falls at the end of S1.

Wrong order. Vladimir and Anatoly lead the Russian Mafia (Veles Taxi) before they become partners in Fisk's alliance. Episode 4 shows their backstory: after escaping a Russian prison they came to New York to build their own operation. Fisk murders Anatoly in episode 5 ('World on Fire'), and Vladimir turns on Fisk and wars against him until he dies in episode 6. As filed, the record never shows that the Mafia came before Fisk. The proposal puts the Mafia first, then Fisk's Empire, then the Mafia again when he turns on Fisk. His last stage is unchanged.

Wrong order. Blake is an NYPD detective at the 15th Precinct, partnered with Hoffman, who goes on Fisk's payroll (episode 6). He is still a cop on Fisk's payroll when Hoffman kills him on Fisk's orders (episode 8). The NYPD came first. As filed, the record starts in Fisk's Empire and then moves to the NYPD. His last stage, Fisk's Empire, is unchanged.

Deadpool & Wolverine: Cassandra is a variant, the twin of her own universe's Charles Xavier. The TVA banished her to the Void as a baby. She is not the main MCU (Earth-199999). Marvel Database files her as Cassandra Nova Xavier (Earth-TRN872), twin of Charles Xavier (Earth-TRN872). The Wolverine variant from the same film is already filed with an Earth (Earth-TRN1400).

Every step on file is the branched Victor. In Loki S2 episode 3, Renslayer slips him the TVA handbook in 1868, which creates a new branch. He shows the Loom at the 1893 fair. In episodes 4-6 he works on the TVA's Loom. Marvel Database files this Victor as Earth-TRN1071 and keeps a separate Earth-199999 Victor: the Sacred Timeline boy who never gets the book, seen in episode 6.

owner_calls.question: Raava serves undercover as James Rhodes all through Secret Invasion. Undercover service counts, but no group name for it is said on screen. Rhodes's own file uses U.S. Air Force. This was already raised as an owner call in rout_34 and is still open. Add an undercover stage?
options: [["The Skrull Rebels","Secret Invasion"],["U.S. Air Force","Secret Invasion"],["The Skrull Rebels","Secret Invasion"]]
A U.S. government stage under a name the owner picks
owner_calls.evidence: Gravik orders Raava to impersonate Rhodes. As 'Colonel Rhodes' she briefs President Ritson (episode 1), speaks for the U.S. at the London summit and fires Fury (episode 2), and pushes Ritson toward war (episode 5). Fury kills her in episode 6.

owner_calls.question: In Secret Invasion episode 3, Pagon gets into the Royal Navy as Lt. Cdr. Dave Matailton aboard HMS Neptune to order a missile strike. Is a one-mission impersonation 'undercover service' (add a Royal Navy stage), or more like a one-job and not counted?
options: Add ["Royal Navy","Secret Invasion"] between Skrull Rebels stages
owner_calls.evidence: Pagon gives Beto and Zirksu their targets, shifts into Matailton at HMNB Clyde, and boards HMS Neptune. The order is overridden. He dies as a Rebel in episode 5.

owner_calls.question: Dox's last stage is Independent, after the TVA locks her up. On screen she leads her own breakaway band of loyalists: they raid the armory in episode 1, prune timelines in episode 2, and are held and killed together in episode 4. Keep Independent, or record the band (the wiki calls it 'Dox's Loyalists'; I can't confirm the screen names it)?
options: Replace Independent with a stage for Dox's loyalists under a name the owner picks
owner_calls.evidence: The TVA arrests Dox for unsanctioned pruning in episode 2. In episode 4 she refuses Renslayer, and Miss Minutes kills her with her loyalists.

owner_calls.question: Should Dex's past job at the suicide hotline be added as a past stage between the U.S. Army and the FBI?
options: Add ["Brooklyn Suicide Prevention Center","Daredevil S3"] after U.S. Army
owner_calls.evidence: Daredevil S3 episode 5 flashback: Dex answers calls ('Suicide Prevention, this is Dex') with Julie Barnes and keeps a staff photo. He worked there about a year after the Army and left after Julie did. The full name 'Brooklyn Suicide Prevention Center' comes from the wiki; I can't confirm the screen shows it.
